back: Arid: typically under about 250 mm of rain a year. Semi-arid: about 250–500 mm. Rainfall is low compared with potential evaporation.
Precipitation ÷ potential evapotranspiration. Hyper-arid below 0.05, arid 0.05–0.20, semi-arid 0.20–0.50.
Low, variable and intense rainfall; very high daytime temperatures; a diurnal range of 20–30 °C; clear skies, low humidity, high evaporation and strong winds.
Air rising at the ITCZ sinks at about 30° (the Hadley cell), warms by compression, so its relative humidity falls and cloud does not form.
A cold current (Benguela, Humboldt, Canary, West Australian) cools the air above it, which is stable and gives fog but no rain: Namib and Atacama.
A dry area on the leeward side of a mountain range where air descends and warms, for example Patagonia behind the Andes.
Remoteness from the sea, giving a large temperature range and little moisture, as in the Gobi and the central Sahara.
56.7 °C at Death Valley, California, in July 1913.
CV (%) = sample standard deviation ÷ mean × 100; a high value shows unreliable rainfall.
